data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The precise distinction is state-convergence versus invariant-preservation: an idempotent operation guarantees identical resulting state after any number of applications, while a safe operation guarantees only that system invariants are not violated \u2014 the state may differ. An append-only log requires safety at the writer level and idempotency at the replay/consumer level, forming a two-layer separation of concerns.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the replay engine cannot distinguish duplicates (no event identifiers), the two-layer separation fails and the system cannot achieve deterministic replay.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If writers themselves enforce deduplication (making append idempotent), the distinction collapses and only the writer layer matters.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If safety invariants include 'no duplicate entries' (a content-uniqueness constraint), then safe-append and idempotent-append coincide, contradicting the claim that they differ.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The writer's contract is to persist an event to the log tail without corrupting existing entries or violating ordering constraints. This is a safety property: even if the same event is appended twice, the log remains well-formed (entries are never mutated or deleted, order is preserved). The state differs (duplicate entries exist), so the writer is not idempotent. The replay engine's contract, by contrast, must be idempotent: re-reading or re-processing a duplicate entry must yield the same resulting state as processing it once. This is achieved by the replay engine maintaining a 'last applied' cursor and skipping events with already-seen identifiers. The causal mechanism is a separation: non-idempotent-but-safe writers + idempotent consumers = deterministic replay under at-least-once delivery.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
